dedupe_keys.name: green roofs on prefabricated housing estates for urban heat island mitigation wrocław

description: A 2021 PLoS ONE study that proposes a three-stage procedure to decide which existing apartment blocks should get green roofs to reduce the urban heat island, and applies it to prefabricated housing estates built in the 1970s and 1980s in Wrocław, Poland. Stage one identifies and classifies buildings by floors and available rooftop area; stage two picks buildings in priority areas with the highest heat island intensity and roof density; stage three analyses roof load capacity to build retrofit scenarios. The authors found 1,962 buildings with 722,405 square metres of roof, of which 480 buildings with 122,749 square metres were selected for greening. The roofs were not designed to carry extra load, so scenario 1 assumes extensive greening after strengthening the ventilated roof and scenario 2 semi-intensive greening after converting it to a non-ventilated roof. The authors, from the Wrocław University of Environmental and Life Sciences and University of Wrocław, say the procedure can be applied to any city with prefabricated blocks and heat island data. Access: open article, CC BY; data are within the paper and supporting files. Caveats: one city, and cooling effects were not simulated. Useful for heat adaptation planning; related records are not yet linked.
